subject: Medicine
summary: Bronchial asthma is a reversible airway disease marked by episodic bronchoconstriction, inflammation, and hyperresponsiveness. Symptoms flare with triggers and improve with bronchodilators. Management focuses on trigger avoidance, inhaled therapy, and monitoring.

sections.p: Asthma is defined by variable airflow limitation that improves with bronchodilators or spontaneously. Diagnosis combines history, peak flow variability, and response to treatment.
b: Exacerbations triggered by allergens, exercise, cold air

t.b: Measures FEV1 and FVC; a reversible drop >12% after bronchodilator confirms asthma.
Daily peak flow variation >20% indicates uncontrolled asthma.
Positive if FEV1 falls 20% at low concentration; used when spirometry is normal but suspicion remains.

sections.p: Severity is staged by symptom frequency and lung function, guiding treatment intensity.
Asthma is multifactorial; the most common triggers are allergens and irritants, followed by infections and occupational exposures.
b: Allergic sensitization (dust mites, pollen, animal dander)

t.b: Identifies IgE-mediated allergens; positive results guide avoidance.
Elevated IgE supports atopy but is not diagnostic alone.

sections.p: Patients report episodic wheeze, chest tightness, cough, and shortness of breath, often worse at night or early morning.
Investigations confirm airflow limitation, assess severity, and rule out mimics.

t.b: Excludes pneumonia, pneumothorax, or structural lung disease.
Elevated eosinophils suggest allergic phenotype; guides biologic therapy.
High FeNO indicates eosinophilic airway inflammation.

sections.p: Severe exacerbations can lead to respiratory failure; chronic disease may cause airway remodeling and fixed obstruction.

t.b: Detects hypoxia or hypercapnia during severe attacks.

whenToSeekHelp: Stridor or severe wheeze not relieved by rescue inhaler

faq.a: Asthma is a chronic condition; control is achieved with long‑term therapy, not cure.
Allergens, viral infections, exercise, cold air, smoke, and occupational irritants.
They reduce airway inflammation, the underlying cause of asthma symptoms.

exam: Explain how reversible airflow limitation is demonstrated on spirometry.
Describe the stepwise approach to asthma management and when to add a long‑acting β2‑agonist.
List common triggers and explain how they precipitate an asthma attack.
